back: A financial statement showing a company's financial position at a specific date.
Based on the equation: $$\text{Assets} = \text{Liabilities} + \text{Owner's Equity}$$
Assets are what the company owns, liabilities what it owes, equity the owner's stake.
Economic resources owned by the company.
[[kw:Current assets]]: convert to cash or used within 1 year (cash, accounts receivable, inventory, prepaid expenses).
[[kw:Plant and equipment]]: long‑term assets used in operations (building, land, machinery).
cards.front: Define [[kw:assets]] and their two main categories.

back: Debts or obligations due within one year.
Examples: accounts payable, salaries payable, short‑term loans.
They are listed on the balance sheet above long‑term liabilities.
$$\text{Owner's Equity} = \text{Total Assets} - \text{Total Liabilities}$$
It represents the net worth of the business.
For a corporation, it's called stockholders' equity (common stock + retained earnings).
Accounts receivable: money owed to the company by customers (asset).
Accounts payable: money the company owes to suppliers (liability).
Both are current items.
cards.front: What is the difference between [[kw:accounts receivable]] and [[kw:accounts payable]]?

back: The cumulative net profits kept in the business rather than distributed to owners.
Part of stockholders' equity.
Not cash; can be invested in assets.
Expresses each item as a percentage of total assets (or total liabilities and equity).
$$\text{Percent} = \frac{\text{Line Item}}{\text{Total Assets}} \times 100$$
Allows comparison of relative size across companies.
cards.front: What is [[kw:vertical analysis]] of a balance sheet?

back: Compares financial data over two or more periods.
Percent change = ((New – Old) / Old) × 100.
Reveals trends and growth patterns.
False. It shows financial position at a specific date (snapshot).
Performance over time is shown on the income statement.
